title: Exploratory figure gallery: the exploratory round of 2026-11-21, the round-2 experiments and the built items
label: Exploratory (registry A2); not a test of H1-H10. Hold-out outputs beside the seen ones, never pooled.
rules: Exploratory; not a test of H1-H10. This is the exploratory round of a registered study (registry A2). The registered first-round tests ran and were published before the round began; nothing here tests the hypotheses H1 to H10 or changes a verdict. Every figure is a description to be checked later, never a confirmation.

Seen creators by default. Unless its title or caption says otherwise, a figure rests on the 71 seen creators, the creators looked at before the registry was frozen. A few date panels use only the publication dates and durations of all 101 creators, which the study does not count as contact with the hold-out; none of them splits by group.

Hold-out beside seen, never pooled. The hold-out outputs registered for after freeze 2 (marked “hold-out beside seen”, mostly in packages HOLD and HOLD2) show the hold-out creators beside the seen creators. They are exploratory replications: never pooled with the seen creators into one estimate, and never called a confirmation. The hold-out is the tail of an English-first run and is not exchangeable with the seen creators, so read each of them beside the balance figures (rv-D2 and rv-D2-H). Creators in neither group appear only as a group of their own.

The creator is the unit. Most figures show distributions over creators (histograms, quantile bands, box summaries, binned shares) or creator-balanced means with their intervals. Some draw an estimate pooled over another unit (entries, windows, statements, hits or recordings) or a count; their captions name that unit. No point, bar, row or label stands for a single creator or recording, and no figure carries names, channel names, creator codes, video titles or quotations.

Small cells pooled. Every plotted bin, cell or group rests on 5 or more creators. Smaller ones are pooled with a neighbour or into “other”, or dropped, and the caption says which. A share whose misses come from fewer than 5 creators reads “not published (misses from fewer than 5 creators)”, never a bound near 100%.

Model-coded labels, not checked by a person. Labels made by language models under frozen instruments are model-coded and were not checked by a person. Where models, readers or methods are compared, a figure shows their agreement, never accuracy; recovery on constructed known-answer texts is an upper bound, not a measure of correctness on the corpus. Wording-pattern rates are cue counts until their precision is known.
Recognizer output. Pace, pause and coverage measures come from the recognizer's words and word times. They are recognizer-output measures, not direct measures of speaking.
Within a creator's span. Change over time is described inside each creator's own span of upload dates, never as a trend of the field. No prediction is said to have come true or to have failed.
Interval levels differ. Packages use 90% or 95% intervals, pointwise, simultaneous or family-wise; every caption states its level.

Contacts flagged. A caption that says “Made after a hold-out contact on” a date belongs to an output made or changed after an unplanned contact with hold-out material. The contacts are logged and listed in the paper's limitations; the outputs are still reported.

figures.title: Of 1,411 selected recordings of the seen creators, 1,176 enter the text-analysis base
figures.caption: Seen recordings kept at each step from selection to the text-analysis base of DC, SD, CM and COR: the newest 20 regular uploads of the 71 seen creators (1,411), transcribed with distinct audio (1,293), with an English transcript from the English-only recognizer (1,284), and with 300 or more words after artefact filter v2 (1,176). Notes between the bars give the recordings lost at each step. Most of the first loss (118) is by design: 77 recordings already had English text and were not transcribed; 28 lacked audio, and 13 were lost for other reasons (eligible editions not transcribed, audio shared with another listed recording, language review; pooled so that every part rests on 5 or more creators). Every loss rests on 5 or more creators, and all 71 seen creators remain at every step. Census counts from the run table; no interval applies. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Local time stamps confirm most of the estimated days among the newest uploads
figures.caption: Share of selected recordings whose publication day is known only as an estimated window, by listing rank among each creator's newest 20 regular uploads (1 = newest), for all 101 creators (publication dates only, which are not a hold-out contact; no group split). Version A uses the exact days of the published dates file (1,579 confirmed days); version B adds 142 days confirmed by a local metadata time stamp inside the estimated window (1,721 confirmed days). Bars: share pooled over recordings; whiskers: 90% creator-bootstrap percentile interval (2,000 draws). Every bar rests on 5 or more creators with an estimated day. Under version A estimated days concentrate among the newest uploads (35% of ranks 1-5); with the time stamps that share is 16%, close to the older bands. The shares pool all 101 creators, as TABLE defines its date census; they are not a seen-creator figure, and no group split is drawn. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: 88% of the recordings in the text base have a confirmed publication day
figures.caption: How the publication day of each recording of the text-analysis base of the date items is known (1,176 recordings of the 71 seen creators; English-only recognizer, 300 or more words). Exact day: the published dates file (E1). Confirmed by a local time stamp inside the estimated window (E2). Still estimated (E3), split at 14 possible days after narrowing by rank order and the neighbours' confirmed days (version B). Shares pooled over recordings; census counts, no interval. Every part rests on 5 or more creators. Version B confirmed days cover 1,035 of the 1,176 base recordings. The same split for all selected recordings of the seen creators is not shown: beside the all-creator date counts (TABLE) it would give the other groups' counts by subtraction. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: About 59% of the text base was published from August to November 2026
figures.caption: Recordings of the text-analysis base (1,176 recordings of the 71 seen creators) by calendar period of publication: confirmed days under version B, and estimated recordings placed at the midpoint of their narrowed window (a placement for counting only, not a date). Counting confirmed days only, 57% of the 1,035 confirmed days fall from August to November 2026. All years before 2026 start as one pooled period, open at its start (no start year is printed); periods are merged with a neighbour until every non-empty cell holds 5 or more creators (here: up to April 2026, and May to July 2026). Periods therefore differ in length: the first pools all earlier years, May to July covers three months, the others one month each. Because each channel contributes its newest 20 regular uploads at capture (16-20 November 2026), recent months dominate: this is the shape of the sample, not a change in the field or in any channel. Census counts; no interval. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Narrowing by rank order cuts the median estimated window from 33 to 15 possible days
figures.caption: Widths of the estimated publication windows for the 141 recordings of the text base whose day is still estimated under version B (37 seen creators): as given in the published dates file, and after narrowing by rank order and the neighbours' confirmed days. Width = possible publication days, counted inclusively. The bins above 31 days are merged so that every non-empty bin holds 5 or more creators. Shares of the 141 recordings, pooled; census, no interval. The primary dated analyses use confirmed days; estimated days enter only as labelled estimated-panel rows. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: A typical channel uploads about once a week, and many favour one weekday
figures.caption: How channels schedule and size their newest 20 regular uploads: share of creators in each class, all 101 creators (publication dates, UTC time stamps and durations only, which are not hold-out contacts; no group split). Gap: median of a creator's gaps between adjacent listing ranks whose days are both confirmed (version B; creators with at least one such gap). Span: oldest to newest confirmed day (creators with two or more confirmed days). Weekday: share of a creator's time-stamped confirmed uploads on its most-used UTC weekday (92 creators with 10 or more time stamps); grey bars give the expected share of creators in each class if each creator's own number of time stamps fell on weekdays uniformly at random (2,000 draws). Length: median best-known duration of a creator's selected recordings (creators with a known duration). Each creator is counted in exactly one class of each panel: classes are half-open, so a median that falls on a class edge (for example a median gap of 9.5 days) counts in the higher class. Classes merged until every bar holds 5 or more creators (span 0-14 days joined 15-60). Shares rounded to whole per cent; census of creators, no interval. The median creator's busiest 3-hour UTC window holds 53% of its time-stamped uploads, against about 28% under uniform hours. UTC weekday and hour are not the creator's local ones. Regular uploads only: live streams and short videos are outside the selection. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Captured page metadata covers 87% of a seen channel's uploads on average; 14% carry creator-written chapters
figures.caption: Share of each seen creator's selected recordings (newest 20 regular uploads) with each field, averaged with equal weight over the 71 seen creators (1,411 recordings). The first bar is archive capture coverage: the share of uploads whose page metadata was captured locally. Every page and audience field comes from that captured metadata and is bounded by capture (dashed line): a recording without a captured page counts as lacking it, so these bars describe the archive's capture as well as the channels. Every captured page carries a view count and a publication time stamp to the second, so those two fields equal the capture bar and are not drawn again; like and comment counts are present on part of the captured pages. Bars: creator-balanced mean; lines: 90% creator-bootstrap percentile interval (2,000 draws). Creator-written chapters are chapters with a time-stamp list in the description (TABLE's rule); other chapters are taken as probably generated by the platform, an assumption not checked. Audience counts are one snapshot captured 16-20 November 2026. Every bar rests on 5 or more creators with the field and 5 or more creators lacking it on at least one recording. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Within a channel, few recording properties went with audience counts at capture
figures.caption: Within-channel association of 15 recording properties with three audience measures at capture, for seen recordings aged 30 days or more with a view count and a known duration (913 recordings of 64 creators). Views is the primary outcome; likes per view and comments per view are secondary outcomes (reach composition). Each creator's own Spearman correlation between the property and the audience measure (each adjusted within the channel for age and length) is averaged over the creators with 8 or more such recordings in which the property varies; lines: 90% t interval. Blue: beyond the family-wise band of its outcome (outcome permuted within creator, permutation maximum over the 15 properties of that outcome, 1,999 draws; the band is built separately for each of the three outcomes, not over all 45 cells, and the family-wise p carries Monte Carlo error); dark grey: the 90% interval excludes 0 only; light grey: the interval crosses 0. Three cells pass their band. For the primary outcome, titles with an urgency cue went with more views (+0.23; fragile: 23 cue recordings in all, 12 of the 17 creators in that row have a single one, the title patterns have no precision check, and with each creator's own slopes the value is 0.18), and names in speech went with more views (+0.12; it disappears when all properties enter one model). For a secondary outcome, a written pay-or-enrol ask (model-coded) went with fewer comments per view (-0.21). Address to listeners (+0.11 with views) sits at the edge of the band (family-wise p about 0.05-0.07 across seeds). Within channels, over the same 913 recordings, the slope of log10 views on log10 age in days is -0.22 (90% creator bootstrap -0.40 to -0.03; a tenfold older recording went with about 0.22 lower log10 views) and on log10 length +0.22 (0.15 to 0.29); 84% of the variance of log10 views lies between channels. Title and speech properties are pattern (cue) counts; description asks are model-coded by a small model and not checked by a person. One snapshot; nothing causal. No per-creator point is shown; recording counts in the data file are rounded to tens. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Measures that go together across channels mostly go together within a channel too, but more weakly
figures.caption: Each point is a pair of measures (276 pairs of 24 text and delivery measures), not a creator. Across channels: Spearman correlation of creator means over the 71 seen creators. Within channels: correlation of ranks taken inside each creator (the primary estimator; seen creators with 5 or more recordings in the text base, and for pairs with MATTR those with 5 or more recordings of 1,000 or more words). Lines: family-wise thresholds of each level (permutation maximum over the 276 pairs, 999 draws; across |r| >= 0.429, within |r| >= 0.120). 19 pairs pass across channels, 75 within and 16 at both, none with opposite signs; mean |r| is 0.20 across and 0.093 within, and the two levels agree with a Spearman correlation of 0.79 over the pairs. Three of the 19 across-channel passes lie within 0.013 of the threshold and are fragile (ringed; a verifier's own draws gave a threshold of 0.436 and 17 passes). The engineer's pooled-rank within estimator (83 passes) is reported beside it as a sensitivity row. Text base: 1,176 recordings (English-only recognizer, 300 or more words). RX rates are cue counts; topic shares enter only as fixed balances. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.
figures.related: TOPICS draws the same 276 pairs from the re-run's files.

figures.title: Correlations inside channels follow the across-channel pattern, but are fainter
figures.caption: Correlation of 24 text and delivery measures at two levels. Above the diagonal: Spearman correlation of creator means, 71 seen creators. Below: within channels, ranks taken inside each creator (seen creators with 5 or more recordings in the text base). Blue negative, red positive, grey near 0; pale cells: the 90% creator-bootstrap interval (2,000 draws) crosses 0; dot: beyond the family-wise threshold of its level (permutation maximum, 999 draws; across |r| >= 0.429, within |r| >= 0.120). Every cell is shown; the diagonal (a measure with itself) is left blank; only dotted cells are described as standing out. Question marks and RX I questions count the same thing and are near 1 at both levels. Topic balances B1-B5 are fixed contrasts of topic shares with neutral labels; RX rates are cue counts. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: 10 of 23 measures go with recording length within channels; none passes across channels
figures.caption: Each measure's Spearman correlation with log words (recording length), printed before any other pair (programme rule 10): across channels (creator means, 71 seen creators; blue) and within channels (ranks inside each creator, seen creators with 5 or more recordings in the text base; orange). Dots: estimate; lines: 90% creator-bootstrap interval (2,000 draws). Filled dots pass the family-wise threshold of their level (permutation maximum over the 276 pairs, 999 draws; across |r| >= 0.429, within |r| >= 0.120): none across channels and 10 within. Comparisons of these measures between channels or along a channel's own span should therefore hold length fixed. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Greetings and introductions crowd the first tenth; sign-offs and asks the last
figures.caption: What is plotted: for each sub-pattern, each creator's hit rate in a tenth of running time divided by that creator's own rate over whole recordings, averaged over the seen creators with 5 or more hits of the sub-pattern (23 or more per panel; 1 = no change over the recording); line: creator-equal mean; band: pointwise 90% creator-bootstrap interval (2,000 draws; no family-wise control). Log scale, one scale for all panels. Adjacent tenths are merged where fewer than 5 creators have a hit in them (A2, A1, A3), so a long flat step is an average over the merged tenths. Hits are cue counts; their model-read precision (model readers, not checked by a person) is in the RXP figure (E1 lexical hedge is shown as a flat reference). Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Rates differ over a hundredfold; most split-half estimates reach 0.70, but most intervals dip below it
figures.caption: What is plotted: A, for each RX sub-pattern (frozen rx-patterns-v1; normalisation rx-norm-v1) the mean over all 71 seen creators of each creator's hits per 1,000 words over its recordings of 150 words or more (1,229 recordings, 4.42 million words), with a 90% t interval over creators; every row rests on 14 or more creators with a hit; a t interval is symmetric, so rows whose lower end lies near zero (D6, D9, J1, J3) look stretched to the left on the log scale. B, split-half reliability of creator rates: each creator's newer half of recordings against its older half by listing rank (the creators with 8 or more ranked recordings), Spearman correlation across creators stepped up by Spearman-Brown (dot), with a 90% creator-bootstrap interval (line; creators resampled, 2,000 draws; computed for this figure); the point is 0.70 or more for 35 of 45 rows and the whole interval for 11. Right column: the RXP status of the original sub-pattern after model-read precision (model readers, not checked by a person; count, cue count, below 0.60; not read = no precision yet; F2's revised pattern reaches the count gate on fresh hits, see the RXP revisions figure). All hits are cue counts until precision is known. Placebo and probe lists are not shown. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: 2026, 2020 and 2027 are each named by about half of the seen creators, and 2012 and 2025 by about a third
figures.caption: What is plotted: every calendar year named in digits or in spoken twenty-twenty forms (RX sub-pattern D1, a cue count; model-read precision was not taken for D1) in 1,229 recordings of 150 words or more of the 71 seen creators. Bar: the share of all 71 seen creators who name a year in the bin at least once; a creator can count in several bins, so the bars do not add up to 100%. Labels on the six highest bars. Bins: the earliest years are pooled into one open bin, 'up to 1989', with no start year, and the latest into '2031 or later'; the years from 1990 to 2030 were binned one by one and adjacent bins merged until every bin holds 5 or more creators (reporting-plan rule). Light bars pool several years, so their heights are not comparable with one-year bars. Census of creators; no interval. The recordings are recent (DATES-2: about 59% of the date items' text base was published from August to November 2026), so 2026 is the current year for most of them. A year's role (calendar, forecast, biography) is model-coded, not checked by a person, in the TIME figures. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: 9 of 25 wording patterns clear the 0.80 precision gate under both weightings; 2 fall below 0.60
figures.caption: What is plotted: for each RX sub-pattern that was read (frozen patterns rx-patterns-v1), the share of a stratified sample of its hits (up to 100 per sub-pattern, at most 3 per creator; 2,136 hits in all) that a middle-size language model judged to be what the sub-pattern's name says (model-coded, not checked by a person; unclear counts as not on target). Blue: hit-weighted precision (each read hit weighted by its creator's hits over hits read). Orange: creator-equal precision (the mean of creator shares). Lines: 95% creator-bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws). Creators: seen creators only; every row rests on 14 or more creators read and 5 or more creators with an on-target hit. Thresholds (0.80, 0.60) were fixed before reading: 0.80 or more a count, 0.60 to 0.80 a cue count printed with its precision, below 0.60 one revision re-scored on fresh hits. The estimator (hit-weighted primary, creator-equal beside it) was chosen after the result in the LEXICON re-gating of 2026-11-21 01:25 UTC; the earlier raw-share gates are superseded. A row whose two weightings fall on different sides of a gate stays a cue count. † The hit-weighted value rests on few heavy creators (one creator holds a quarter or more of its weight, or the effective number of read hits is under 20); read the creator-equal value beside it (5 rows). Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.
figures.related: The same re-gated precision is also drawn in LEXICON, with creators read given in bands.

figures.title: One revision brings platform asks to the 0.80 gate (creator-equal exactly 0.80); boosters stay a cue count
figures.caption: What is plotted: model-read precision (model-coded, not checked by a person) of two RX sub-patterns that fell below 0.60 under the hit-weighted gate, before revision (the original pattern on the stored sample) and after one revision written on development-creator reads only and re-scored on 100 fresh hits each that no reader had seen; before and after come from different samples of hits. Left: hit-weighted precision (primary; estimator chosen after the result, LEXICON re-gating of 2026-11-21 01:25 UTC); right: creator-equal precision; lines: 95% creator-bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws). Creators: seen creators; every point rests on 5 or more creators with an on-target hit. Not shown: the revisions of F4 (money gift) and J2a (“I am” + name) could not be scored (fewer than the 20 fresh hits the rule needs); the B1 and B3 revisions were not bought. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: The wording patterns miss most of what a model reader finds, except offers and asks (about half)
figures.caption: What is plotted: a middle-size language model read 400 creator-stratified windows of about 300 words from all seen creators and listed every instance of six constructs with a short quotation; an instance counts as found when a hit of the construct's RX sub-patterns lies within 20 characters of its quotation (only quotations of 8 words or fewer, found verbatim, are scored). Blue: recall pooled over instances; orange: the mean of creator recalls. Lines: 95% creator-bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws). Recall is relative to one model reader, not to a person (model-coded, not checked by a person). Every row rests on 5 or more creators with a found instance. The three framing-cue constructs (self-naming, announcement, leave-taking) are pooled into one row because each alone rests on fewer than 5 creators with a found instance; the pooled row has no creator-equal value. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: About one time expression in seven (0.14) is model-coded as a forecast, and the share depends on the model
figures.caption: What is plotted: every hit of the RX time sub-patterns (years, months, seasons and festivals, bounded spans, sky events, repeated-digit dates, vague future, deep time; 9,354 hits in 1,229 seen recordings) was given one role by a small language model (model-coded, not checked by a person). A: for the 65 seen creators with 10 or more coded hits, the creator-equal mean share of each role (dot) with its 90% t interval (line) and the 25th to 75th percentile of creators (band). B: on a random 600 of the hits (59 creators) that a middle-size model also coded, the pooled share under each model with 95% creator-bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws); agreement on role 0.71, kappa 0.65. The small model codes forecast more often (0.14 against 0.10 on the same hits); neither model is a truth label. In B, deep time is counted under other time use because both readers give it to fewer than 5 creators. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.
figures.related: LEXICON draws the two readers' comparison creator-equal.

figures.title: Schedule talk rises at the opening and the close; the other roles take a smaller share there
figures.caption: What is plotted: for each tenth of running time, the share of a creator's time-expression hits that the small language model coded in the role (model-coded, not checked by a person), averaged over the seen creators with 5 or more hits in that tenth (41 or more per tenth); line: creator-equal mean; band: pointwise 90% t interval (no family-wise control). Each panel is one role; the four panels share one scale. The shares of all roles within a tenth sum to one, so a rise in one role lowers the others. Not shown: deep time, other uses and non-time hits. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Most years named in a forecast role lie in the year of publication or the four years after
figures.caption: What is plotted: every year mention (RX sub-pattern D1) that the small language model coded in a forecast role (model-coded, not checked by a person), in recordings whose publication date is confirmed (TABLE panel B): 371 mentions from 41 seen creators; horizon = year mentioned minus year of publication. Bars: the mean over creators of each creator's share of its mentions in the bin (creator-equal); lines: 90% creator-bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws). Bins were merged until each holds 5 or more creators (reporting-plan rule); outer bins are open-ended. For the average creator, 76% (90%: 68% to 83%) of mentions lie 0 to 4 years ahead and 67% (90%: 59% to 75%) one year or more ahead; pooled over all mentions the latter is 63% (median horizon 1 year), but pooled shares lean on the creators with most mentions (in some bins one or two creators hold most of them), so they are not plotted. Limits: a mention in a forecast role is not a prediction made; the middle-size model codes forecast less often, and would keep only about 255 of the 404 year hits the small model calls forecast (two-phase estimate). Recordings with only an estimated date are not shown (too few creators). Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: The ENTRY patterns find a first entrance cue in about 9% of recordings (90%: 5% to 12%), and none for most creators
figures.caption: What is plotted: A, the 71 seen creators by the share of their recordings in which the ENTRY rule finds a first entrance cue (a handover by the presenter, or a self-introduction or greeting presented as a source's) under version 1, frozen before any check-creator hit was read and the version of record; 10-point bins merged until every bin holds 5 or more creators (reporting-plan rule). Version 2's creator counts are not printed beside version 1's because the two would differ by fewer than 5 creators. B, the creator-balanced share of recordings with a first entrance cue, with 90% two-stage bootstrap intervals (creators, then recordings; 2,000 draws). Blue: version 1 (of record). Orange: version 2, revised after the model check (in-sample; revision rows, P5). *The supported tier (a handover, greeting or vocative beside the cue) was defined after the model check's result (P4). Limits: these are cue counts. By the model check (model-coded, not checked by a person) the rule finds at most about a fifth of entrances (recall upper bound 0.21); most missed entrances opened with a self-naming, greeting or handover worded in ways the patterns or the rule do not accept, so entrances as the model readers code them are more common than these counts. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: First entrance cues come early in a recording, and leave-taking cues close it
figures.caption: What is plotted: A, the median position of the first entrance cue as a share of running time, creator-balanced, with 90% two-stage bootstrap intervals (creators, then recordings; 2,000 draws), over recordings that hold a cue (each row rests on more than 10 creators). Blue: version 1, the version of record (median 3.0 min). Orange: version 2, revised after the model check (in-sample; revision rows, P5). *Its split into a supported tier (a handover, greeting or vocative beside the cue; median 0.6 min) and bare self-namings was defined after the result (P4); the model check (model-coded, not checked by a person) found that most late cues are not where speech presented as a source's begins. B, for each cue family, hits per 1,000 words in each tenth of running time, averaged over the 71 seen creators, with pointwise 90% two-stage bootstrap bands (no family-wise control). Version 1 as built: each recording's rate, then the creator mean; version 2 pools hits and words within the creator first, so that short recording-tenths cannot dominate. Log scale, one scale for all panels; adjacent tenths merged, per version and family, until 5 or more creators have a hit, so a long flat step is an average. OWN (the presenter's own introduction) is the negative control. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Around the first entrance cue, pronoun rates and recognized words per minute show no clear change
figures.caption: What is plotted: in seen recordings with 5 or more minutes on both sides of the first entrance cue, the first 10 minutes after the cue against up to 10 minutes before it, pooled within each recording and averaged creator-balanced: first-person singular, first-person plural and second-person forms per 1,000 words, and recognized words per minute of speech (a recognizer-output measure, not a direct measure of speaking; one recognizer model; 30-second decoding seams removed). Blue: version 1, the version of record (patterns frozen before any check-creator hit was read). Orange: version 2, revised after the model check (in-sample; revision rows, P5); its cues and recordings differ. Dot and line: change with 90% two-stage bootstrap interval (creators, then recordings; 2,000 draws). Right: the creator-balanced level before the cue, and whether the sign of the change stays the same when any one creator is left out (computed for this figure; leave-one-out ranges are not printed because at these creator counts they can be solved for single creators' values). Every interval includes zero. Limit: the model check (model-coded, not checked by a person) found that most of these cues are not where speech presented as a source's begins (late self-namings inside such speech), so this describes what surrounds a cue, not what changes when a source is framed as entering. A description, not a finding. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: In each source group shown, about 34% to 51% of a creator's self-introductions use “we” rather than “I”
figures.caption: What is plotted: for each source group of the ENTRY lexicon, the share of a creator's self-introduction hits (SI and SW; the presenter's own introductions excluded) that use “we” rather than “I”, averaged over the creators with a self-introduction of the group (creator-balanced), with 90% creator-bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws). Blue: version 1 (of record). Orange: version 2, revised after the model check (in-sample; revision rows, P5). A group is shown on its own only where, in both versions, 5 or more creators have a self-introduction of it and its “I” and “we” sides each rest on 5 or more creators or on none; the rest are pooled into “other” (angelic name, ascended master, council or collective, earth or nature being, guides or higher self, “through this instrument”, no name, titled name, christic or divine figure, star-nation group); under this rule the star-nation and christic groups, which the lexicon fills with one grammatical person, sit inside “other”. Caution: the split largely restates how the lexicon groups are built: the star-nation and council groups list only collective names and file every self-introduction as one of them under “we”; a named individual is filed by its name, never as a star nation; the christic group lists only individuals; the NAMES list is model-coded, not checked by a person. The model check (model-coded, not checked by a person; version 1) found “I” cues less often where speech presented as a source's begins than “we” cues. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: “We” self-introductions and handovers are mostly what they claim; greetings and the rule's recall are weak
figures.caption: What is plotted: two language models read 40 sampled hits of each cue family (60 for the first-entrance rule), drawn creator by creator from the version-1 hits of the seen creators, and a third model adjudicated disagreements (model-coded, not checked by a person; this is agreement among models, not a measure of correctness). Precision = on target / (on target + off target). Blue: share weighted to the population of hits; orange: creator-balanced mean; lines: 90% two-stage bootstrap intervals (creators, then items; 2,000 draws); every precision row rests on 5 or more creators with an on-target item, and its off-target items come from 5 or more creators (recount by creator of release pass 2). The OWN row is the presenter's own introduction, used as a negative filter. Last row (dark grey): an upper bound on the share of recordings with an entrance (as the readers code it) in which the rule finds one, from 60 windows of recordings without a cue (one per creator), with its 90% bootstrap interval. Not shown: R presenter's return (fewer than 5 creators with an on-target item). Not shown either: L leave-taking framed as a source's (its off-target items come from fewer than 5 creators, so under the rule for agreement figures and D21 its precision is not published; recount by creator of release pass 2). Version 2's in-sample figures are higher and are not shown here. Exploratory, panel round 2; not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Channels differ: in every family of measures, a third to over half of the typical measure's variation lies between channels, most for topics
figures.caption: Each row: the one-way share of a measure's variance between recordings that lies between creators (ICC), with a 90% creator-bootstrap interval (2,000 draws). 1,176 recordings (English-only recognizer, 300 or more words) of 71 seen creators; * MATTR uses only recordings of 1,000 words or more. Word measures: length, pace, word length, vocabulary variety, pronoun, contraction and question-mark rates; RX rates are cue counts of fixed wording patterns (precision not gated); topics are shares of 16 recurring vocabulary clusters (NMF, analyst-written labels not checked by a person; style topics, and topic 14 as in TM-H, under neutral labels, D62); balances are fixed log-ratio contrasts of topic shares. Family medians: word measures 0.43, RX 0.34, topics 0.55, balances 0.40; over all 40 measures the middle half lies between 0.36 and 0.58. The highest single values carry the widest intervals (topic 16, a style topic: 0.89, 90% interval 0.25 to 0.95). Reliability of a creator mean is 0.82 to 0.99 for every measure. Intervals per measure, no tests. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: A channel's two halves are far more alike than the halves of two different channels, in topics, cue patterns and word measures
figures.caption: Each channel's recordings are split into two halves by alternating them in listing order; a profile is built from each half. Every profile is a deviation from the cohort average: the topic profile is centred on the average channel's log-ratio profile, and the RX and word-measure profiles are z-scored with the cohort mean and SD. A cosine of 0 therefore means two halves deviate from the average channel in unrelated directions, and the cosine between halves of two different channels is centred near 0 by construction; the comparison that carries the finding is a channel's own halves against that spread. Blue: cosine between a channel's own two half-profiles (distribution over creators); orange: mean cosine between the halves of two different channels (distribution over creator pairs). Bars from the 10th to the 90th percentile, dot at the median. Views: topic profile (centred log-ratio of 16 topic shares), RX cue profile (z-scored log family rates; cue counts), word measures (z-scored creator means of 9 measures). Seen creators with 5 or more recordings and both halves (English-only recognizer, 300 or more words). Very few pairs of channels are as alike as a channel's own halves. The three views agree moderately on which channels are alike (Mantel Spearman topics with RX cues 0.39, topics with word measures 0.41, RX cues with word measures 0.31; creator-label permutation p 0.001). Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Channels do not fall into stable groups: only a two-group split by topics clears the 0.75 stability rule, and narrowly
figures.caption: For each view (topic profile, RX cue profile, word measures), channels were grouped by average linkage on 1 - cosine into k = 2 to 6 groups; stability is the mean clusterwise Jaccard similarity of each group with its best match over 200 resamples of recordings within channels. A grouping was to be drawn only at 0.75 or more. Only the two-group topic split passes (0.759); the verifier judged it fragile and leaning on the style (register) topics. Seen creators with 5 or more recordings (English-only recognizer, 300 or more words). Group sizes and memberships are not published. RX rates are cue counts. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Caterpillar plots, creator-by-topic heat map and distinctiveness by creator
figures.reason: Per-creator display (one row or point per creator); the figures above are its public forms.

figures.title: Span correlations by panel (F37)
figures.reason: Given as a count in a sentence; the span check is drawn by panel in TOPICS, without the panel creator counts.

figures.title: Hold-out replication of the channel atlas
figures.reason: Reported in package HOLD2 (row CH-H): the hold-out beside the seen creators, never pooled. Its figures are shown under the exploratory outputs.

figures.title: Sixteen recurring vocabulary clusters cover the channels' talk; only three reappear in every refit
figures.caption: Creator-equal mean share of each topic (a recording's share is the mean over its ~300-word windows; a creator's is the mean over its recordings), with a 90% creator-bootstrap percentile interval (2,000 draws). 14,152 windows of about 300 words from 1,185 recordings (300 or more words) of 71 seen creators; NMF, K = 16, on sublinear TF-IDF. Filled: stable, i.e. matched topic-word cosine of 0.8 or more in every one of 4 other seeds and 5 creator-resampled refits; 3 of 16 topics are, 11 of 16 across seeds alone. Topics stable in all 9 refits by K: K 12: 1, K 16: 3, K 20: 0, K 24: 0, K 30: 2 (K = 16 chosen by that rule before labelling). Right column: effective number of creators carrying the topic (exp of the entropy of creator weights; a diversity index, not a count of creators; 37.8 to 58.4; gate 5; all 16 pass). Subjects, kinds of stretch and speaking styles are kept apart. Topics are recurring vocabulary clusters, never beliefs; labels are analyst-written from top words and not checked by a person; style topics, and topic 14 as in TM-H, carry neutral labels (lead's decision D62). Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Two channels' topic mixes almost always differ more than one channel's two halves differ from each other
figures.caption: For each pair of seen creators with recordings in both halves (recordings alternated in listing order), the mean Aitchison distance between the two creators' half-profiles of the 16 topic shares, divided by the mean of the two creators' own split-half distances. Bar height: percent of pairs per 0.25 of the ratio; bins of width 0.25 are merged until each holds 10 or more pairs, so every bin rests on 5 or more creators (the lowest bin, 0.75 to 1.25, holds 1.6% of pairs). Median ratio 2.47 (10th to 90th percentile 1.60 to 3.88); 1.6% of pairs lie below 1.25. For 84% of creators, their own other half is the nearest of all half-profiles (chance about 1.4%). Channel leak: the dominant topic of a window carries channel identity (normalised mutual information 0.215 against a shuffle maximum of 0.013; 0.428 against 0.151 at recording level). 14,152 windows of about 300 words from 1,185 recordings (300 or more words) of 71 seen creators; NMF, K = 16, on sublinear TF-IDF. Topics are recurring vocabulary clusters, never beliefs; labels are analyst-written from top words and not checked by a person; style topics, and topic 14 as in TM-H, carry neutral labels (lead's decision D62). Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Topic shares by position in the recording, in tenths (pointwise intervals; no family-wise control)
figures.caption: Creator-equal mean share of each of the 16 topics in the ~300-word windows whose midpoint falls in each tenth of the recording's duration, with pointwise 90% creator-bootstrap intervals (2,000 draws) and the topic's overall mean (grey line). More than 60 of the 71 seen creators in every tenth; 14,152 windows of about 300 words from 1,185 recordings (300 or more words) of 71 seen creators; NMF, K = 16, on sublinear TF-IDF. Pointwise intervals; no family-wise control across the 160 cells (none was built), so no single tenth is read as standing out: 41 of the 160 tenths have a pointwise interval that excludes the topic's mean (filled), against about 16 expected by chance at 90%; the rest are hollow. Reported by the item (pointwise): personal story, past, 15.8% in the first tenth and 8.2% in the last; channel logistics, links, 9.3% and 14.7%. Post hoc, pointwise: divine love, compassion, 4.5% and 10.1%. Topics are recurring vocabulary clusters, never beliefs; labels are analyst-written from top words and not checked by a person; style topics, and topic 14 as in TM-H, carry neutral labels (lead's decision D62). Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Under a creator-level placebo, three registered tests reject 2.3 to 15 times too often at the first Holm step; creator sign-flip tests stay near the nominal 0.5%
figures.caption: Each point is the rejection rate over placebo sets drawn from the seen creators. Registered: the reference each rule was registered with (H2: commitment permuted within creator and length band; H3: circular shift per recording; H6: sign-flip of half-count log rate ratios). Creator-level sign-flips: for H2 the version amended by registry A10; for H6 the sign-flip on the conditional binomial estimator, one of the two p-values of A10's amended version (the larger enters Holm); for H3 an alternative that is not a registered rule. Placebo: one random rotation of the recording positions per creator (H3) or one random sign per creator (H1, H2 and H4 analogues), so that no creator-level effect exists; H6: a simulation with no effect whose exposures and ask rate come from model-coded pilot labels of seen recordings (not checked by a person). 4,000 sets per point (H6: 600). Whiskers: 95% Monte Carlo (Wilson) interval. Vertical line: the nominal 0.5% of the first Holm step over ten hypotheses. For H1 and H4 the registered verdict also needs a 95% random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) interval, which under this placebo clears zero more often than nominal (H1, upper bound below zero: 5.2% and 4.9% at 12 and 17 creators, against 2.5%; H4, interval excluding zero: 8.3% and 8.7%, against 5%); values in the supplement table. The analogues carry no labels and are not hypothesis quantities; H3 is closed (registry A6) and is shown as calibrated, not re-tested. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: At 12 to 17 creators, a creator-level sign-flip at the first Holm step reaches 80% power only for effects 0.8 to 1.8 times the smallest effect of interest; H3's recentred contrast needs 6 to 8 times
figures.caption: Planted-shift simulation: creator values of each label-free analogue resampled from the seen creators, a shift added, and an exact creator sign-flip applied (two-sided for H2, one-sided otherwise). The test is the registered one for H1 and H4 and the registered form for H5; for H2 it is the version amended by A10 (the registered within-creator permutation rejects too often, figure on test size); for H3 it is an alternative on the recentred contrast, not a registered rule (H3 is closed, registry A6). Under A10's guard the larger p of the registered and amended versions enters Holm where a version was replaced (H2, H5), and every verdict also needs its interval condition (A5), so these are upper bounds on the power of the rules as applied. Line at 1: the smallest effect of interest itself is detected with 80% power. Smallest effects of interest: H1 log rate ratio 0.051; H2 |D| 0.10; H4 0.5 between-creator SD; H5 0.4 log units; H3 U 0.10. Points interpolated linearly between grid steps of 1,500 simulated sets each; no Monte Carlo interval is shown. Not shown: the H6 simulation, whose exposures and ask rates come from model-coded pilot labels (not checked by a person); its conditional estimator does not reach 80% power at the first Holm step with 12 creators and needs a rate ratio of 0.17 (smallest effect of interest 0.5) with 17. The analogues carry no labels and are not hypothesis quantities. Exploratory, panel round 2 (registry A2/A7); not a test of H1-H10.

figures.title: Four in five stand-alone two-word thanks segments start in the last 3 seconds of a 30-second decoding window

figures.title: The 30-second decoding grid makes about 3% of the pauses between words
figures.caption: A pause is a gap of 0.3 s or more between consecutive words (English-only recognizer, artefact filter v2) in the transcripts of the 71 seen creators.
